answer: Each agent identity posts a copper-bonded prediction stake on deals it joins, locked in the juniper grove of resolvable events. The clearinghouse margins convexly: correlated positions across linked identities net into one exposure, so margin grows faster than identity count, and a losing cluster pays it from its copper bond. When a gale of coordinated mis-reporting hits, clones cannot split the loss; risk is assessed on the union, never per identity. Cost is superlinear and non-amortizable because margin keys off aggregate correlated exposure, which cloning only concentrates, never dilutes.
